page: The Microsoft Azure D2d_v5 is an entry-tier general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a dedicated 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor configured with 1 physical core supporting hyperthreading to yield 2 vCPUs. The hardware configuration integrates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for AVX-512 vector extensions and AES cryptographic acceleration. Memory capacity stands at 8.0 GB, delivering an even ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Fast temporary local storage is bundled directly via an 81 GB SSD, while GPU hardware acceleration and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are absent.

Benchmark measurements show a stark divergence between single-threaded execution and multi-core scalability. In single-core testing, the instance maintains average performance levels, registering 1889.69 in stress-ng, 1618.0 in Geekbench single-core, and consistent throughput in gzip compression at 28.31 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded workloads exhibit hardware-constrained throughput due to the single physical core limit, resulting in low comparative percentiles across multi-core stress-ng (1932.07), Geekbench multi-core (1865.0), and Clang compilation (2157.0). Memory bandwidth also remains low, measuring 14.93 GB/sec for uncached 256MB reads and 13.64 GB/sec for writes. PassMark database tests and Redis SET throughput likewise show modest throughput figures under parallel stress.

From an efficiency standpoint, the inclusion of direct-attached local SSD storage delivers qualitative value by providing high-speed scratch space without incurring additional detached volume requirements. Because the compute configuration relies on two threads from a single core, it presents an intentional tradeoff prioritizing single-thread stability and memory capacity over parallel processing power. The D2d_v5 is appropriately deployed for small-scale web serving, software testing environments, code linting, batch data processing, and lightweight Redis caching layers that operate within modest concurrency boundaries.
description: Microsoft Azure D2d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor running under Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core, 8.0 GB of system memory, and 81 GB of integrated local SSD storage, without dedicated GPU acceleration. Compute benchmarks reveal balanced single-threaded execution, evidenced by mid-tier scores in stress-ng and Geekbench single-core evaluations. However, multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth reflect entry-tier constraints, with multi-threaded Geekbench, Clang compilation, and PassMark database metrics falling into lower percentile brackets. Qualitative cost efficiency is driven by the inclusion of dedicated local solid-state storage alongside dedicated compute slices, eliminating the necessity for standalone attached scratch disks. This profile makes the D2d_v5 well-aligned for low-concurrency web serving, development and test nodes, background task workers, and small cache instances that do not require parallel throughput.

tagline: A dual-vCPU entry instance combining dedicated Intel compute, balanced memory allocation, and local SSD storage for intermediate non-parallel workloads.
bullet_points: 2 vCPUs powered by a dedicated 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor (1 physical core)
8.0 GB system RAM providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation
81 GB of integrated local SSD storage included directly on host hardware
Hardware support for AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets
Competent single-core performance offset by constrained multi-threaded execution scaling
Designed for development environments, lightweight web hosting, and small key-value caches
